about: Labelled samples for the curriculum packs' subject areas, beyond the five in samples.json. Subjects are topic names from FolioKit's Topics.json. All text is original.

samples.subject: Biology
samples.body:
Sexual reproduction combines gametes from two parents, while asexual reproduction produces clones.
Meiosis halves the chromosome number and crossing over shuffles alleles between homologous chromosomes.
Use a Punnett square to predict genotype and phenotype ratios for a cross between two heterozygous parents.
A recessive allele only shows in the phenotype when the organism is homozygous.
Pedigrees show how sex-linked traits such as colour blindness pass down a family.
samples.title: Module 5: Heredity

samples.subject: Biology
samples.body:
1. Label the phospholipid bilayer, channel proteins and carrier proteins on the diagram of the cell membrane.
2. Explain why osmosis moves water into a red blood cell placed in distilled water.
3. Compare active transport with facilitated diffusion, naming which one uses ATP from cellular respiration.
4. Predict what happens to plant cells in a concentrated salt solution, using the word plasmolysis.
samples.title: Movement across the cell membrane

samples.subject: Biology
samples.body:
Aim: to measure how temperature affects the activity of the enzyme catalase found in potato tissue.
Method: add potato discs to hydrogen peroxide in water baths at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 degrees and count the oxygen bubbles released in two minutes.
Results show activity rising to an optimum near 37 degrees, then falling as the enzyme's active site is denatured.
Discuss how the shape of the active site explains the lock-and-key model.
samples.title: Effect of temperature on catalase

samples.subject: Biology
samples.body:
Time allowed: 1 hour 45 minutes
Instructions: Use black ink or black ball-point pen. Answer all questions in the spaces provided.
Topics: cell biology, organisation, infection and response, and bioenergetics.
01.1 Name the organelle where photosynthesis takes place.
01.2 Describe how a vaccine prepares the immune system to produce antibodies against a pathogen.
samples.title: GCSE BIOLOGY Higher Tier Paper 1

samples.subject: Biology
samples.body:
Paper 4 Theory (Extended) May/June 2023. 1 hour 15 minutes.
You must answer on the question paper. Answer all questions.

(b) Explain how natural selection can lead to antibiotic resistance in a population of bacteria.

samples.body:

samples.subject: Earth and Environmental Science
samples.body:
The lithosphere is broken into tectonic plates that move over the mantle.
At subduction zones an oceanic plate sinks beneath another plate, forming volcanic arcs and deep earthquakes.
Mid-ocean ridges form where plates diverge and new crust is made.
The rock cycle links igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks through weathering, erosion, melting and pressure.
samples.title: Plate tectonics

samples.subject: Earth and Environmental Science
samples.body:
Use the ice core data to explain how atmospheric carbon dioxide has changed over the last 800,000 years.
Describe the greenhouse effect and the role of the carbon cycle in climate change.
Evaluate one strategy for reducing reliance on fossil fuels, such as renewable energy.
Due date: end of week 6. Include a graph of global temperature anomalies.
samples.title: Climate science research task

samples.subject: Science
samples.body:
A hypothesis is a testable prediction about the relationship between an independent variable and a dependent variable.
Controlled variables are kept the same so the investigation is a fair test.
Accuracy describes how close a measurement is to the true value; precision describes how close repeated results are to each other.
Reliability improves with repeated trials, and validity depends on measuring what you set out to measure.
Random error and systematic error affect results in different ways.
samples.title: The scientific method

samples.subject: Science
samples.body:
Week 2: refined the inquiry question and wrote the risk assessment.
Week 3: collected primary data from five trials and recorded uncertainty for each measurement.
Week 4: drew a line of best fit and identified one outlier caused by a timing error.
Next step: compare primary data with secondary data from the peer-reviewed article and write the scientific report.
samples.title: Depth study logbook

samples.subject: Psychology
samples.body:
The multi-store model describes sensory memory, short-term memory and long-term memory as separate stores.
Short-term memory holds about seven items for around 18 seconds unless information is rehearsed.
The working memory model adds a central executive, the phonological loop and the visuospatial sketchpad.
The hippocampus is involved in consolidating new long-term memories, while the amygdala adds emotional significance.
samples.title: Models of memory

samples.subject: Psychology
samples.body:
1. Explain why participants must give informed consent and have the right to withdraw.
2. Milgram's obedience study used deception. Evaluate whether the debriefing was enough to protect participants.
3. Zimbardo's prison study raised questions about harm. Identify two ethical guidelines it broke.
4. Distinguish between a correlation and an experiment that shows cause and effect.
samples.title: Ethics in psychological research

samples.subject: Psychology
samples.body:
Neurons communicate across the synapse using neurotransmitters such as dopamine and serotonin.
The cerebral cortex is divided into lobes, and neuroplasticity lets the brain reorganise after injury.
Sleep moves through NREM stages and REM sleep in roughly 90-minute cycles.
Know the difference between sensation and perception for the unit test.
samples.title: Biological bases of behaviour review

samples.subject: Geography
samples.body:
Mumbai is a megacity whose rapid urbanisation has been driven by rural to urban migration.
Informal settlements such as Dharavi show the challenges of providing infrastructure, water and sanitation.
Urban sprawl and gentrification are reshaping land use on the city's edges and in older suburbs.
This essay evaluates how planning strategies affect liveability and sustainable development.
samples.title: Urban dynamics in a megacity

samples.subject: Geography
samples.body:

Explain how coastal erosion and deposition have shaped the landforms you recorded.
samples.title: Coastal landforms fieldwork

samples.subject: Economics
samples.body:
Market failure occurs when the free market allocates resources inefficiently.
Negative externalities such as pollution mean the social cost is greater than the private cost.
Public goods are non-excludable and non-rivalrous, so the market under-provides them.
Governments respond with taxation, subsidies, regulation and tradable permits.
samples.title: Market failure

samples.subject: Economics
samples.body:
Inflation has risen above the Reserve Bank's target band of 2 to 3 per cent.
This essay analyses how monetary policy, through changes to the cash rate and interest rates, reduces aggregate demand.
It also considers the trade-off with unemployment and economic growth, and the role of fiscal policy in the budget.
Conclusion: a coordinated policy mix is most effective in the current business cycle.
samples.title: Managing inflation

Operations management transforms inputs into outputs through the transformation process.
Key influences include globalisation, technology, quality expectations and corporate social responsibility.
Strategies: outsourcing, supply chain management, inventory control and quality management.
Stakeholders such as shareholders, employees and customers judge performance differently.

samples.subject: Business

2. Complete the cash flow forecast for a sole trader over three months.

4. Suggest two ways the business could improve cash flow.

samples.subject: Accounting
samples.body:

samples.subject: Accounting
samples.body:
Depreciation spreads the cost of a non-current asset over its useful life.
Straight-line depreciation charges the same amount each year; reducing balance charges more in early years.
Accrual accounting records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, not when cash moves.
The balance sheet shows accumulated depreciation against the asset's original cost.
samples.title: Depreciation and accrual accounting

samples.subject: Legal Studies
samples.body:
Police powers include arrest, search and seizure, and questioning, balanced against the rights of suspects.
Bail may be granted or refused under the Bail Act, considering the risk of reoffending.
The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt in the court hierarchy, from the Local Court to the High Court.
Sentencing aims include deterrence, rehabilitation and community protection.
samples.title: Crime: the criminal investigation process

samples.subject: Legal Studies
samples.body:
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights set out rights that are now protected in international law.
This essay evaluates the effectiveness of the United Nations, courts and non-government organisations in enforcing human rights.
It examines the rule of law and the role of legislation in protecting rights domestically.
Law reform has been slow where state sovereignty limits international enforcement.
samples.title: Promoting and enforcing human rights

samples.subject: Legal Studies
samples.body:

samples.subject: Politics
samples.body:
State sovereignty means a state has supreme authority within its borders.
Legitimacy can come from elections, constitutions or international recognition.
International relations are shaped by the United Nations, NATO and other intergovernmental organisations.
Diplomacy and foreign policy are the main tools states use to pursue their interests.

samples.subject: Studies of Religion
samples.body:
The Buddha taught the Four Noble Truths: suffering, its cause, its end and the path to its end.
The Noble Eightfold Path guides ethics, mental discipline and wisdom.
Karma and rebirth continue until enlightenment ends the cycle of samsara.
Buddhist ethics include the Five Precepts followed by adherents.

samples.subject: Studies of Religion
samples.body:
Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that every able Muslim should make once in their life.
Pilgrims perform rituals such as circling the Kaaba and standing at Arafat in prayer.
The practice expresses beliefs found in the Quran about submission to God and the unity of the ummah.
Daily prayer, fasting during Ramadan and worship at the mosque are other pillars.
samples.title: Islam: a significant practice

samples.subject: Philosophy
samples.body:

Knowledge question: to what extent do the methods of an area of knowledge shape what counts as knowledge?

Claim and counterclaim, with real-life examples, then a conclusion about justified true belief.
samples.title: TOK essay plan

samples.subject: Philosophy
samples.body:
Utilitarianism judges actions by their consequences: the greatest good for the greatest number.
Kant's deontology says some duties hold whatever the consequences, using the categorical imperative.
Virtue ethics, from Aristotle, asks what a person of good character would do.
A thought experiment such as the trolley problem tests each theory.
samples.title: Normative ethics

samples.subject: Health and Physical Education
samples.body:
The ATP-PC system supplies energy for about 10 seconds of maximal effort.
Anaerobic glycolysis produces lactate and fuels efforts of up to two minutes.
The aerobic system uses oxygen and dominates longer activities; VO2 max measures aerobic capacity.
Training adaptations depend on the energy system that the sport relies on.
samples.title: Energy systems

samples.subject: Health and Physical Education
samples.body:

Include a warm-up and cool-down, target heart rate zones and fitness testing before and after.
Evaluate how the program improves skill acquisition and performance.
samples.title: Training program for improved performance

samples.subject: Health and Physical Education
samples.body:
The Ottawa Charter's five action areas guide health promotion: building healthy public policy, creating supportive environments, strengthening community action, developing personal skills and reorienting health services.
The determinants of health include individual, sociocultural, socioeconomic and environmental factors.
Risk factors and health behaviours explain differences in the burden of disease.
samples.title: Health promotion and the Ottawa Charter

samples.subject: Visual Arts
samples.body:
Frida Kahlo's paintings use her own image to explore identity, pain and Mexican culture.

samples.subject: Visual Arts

Impressionism began in Paris in the 1870s with painters such as Monet, Renoir and Morisot.
Artists painted outdoors to capture changing light, using visible brushstrokes and bright colour.
The movement broke with the Salon and led towards Modernism and later Cubism.
Compare Monet's water lilies with a Renaissance landscape in your art criticism.
samples.title: Art history: Impressionism
